title: Department of Labor Open Data API (OSHA, WHD, ETA unemployment claims, MSHA)
questions: OSHA inspections and penalties for a company
serious OSHA violations in a state
back wages recovered by the Wage and Hour Division in an industry

key_only: every data query (only the dataset catalog and field dictionaries are keyless)

manual.how: Open each link in manual_download/INSTRUCTIONS.md in a browser after replacing {API_KEY} with your own DOL API key (free: register at https://dataportal.dol.gov/registration, then copy a key from https://dataportal.dol.gov/api-keys), or run download_data.sh / download_data.ps1 (one command; asks for the key with hidden input); save each JSON file under the name shown, upload them, then --ingest. Without the bundle: open the dataset in the Data Catalog (https://dataportal.dol.gov/datasets), use the API Query Builder at the bottom of the page (signed in) to set filters and download the response, or use the agency's own downloads (OSHA: https://www.osha.gov/data; WHD: https://enforcedata.dol.gov; weekly claims: https://oui.doleta.gov/unemploy/claims.asp); upload the file and say which it is.

cache.why: Enforcement datasets are reloaded daily to quarterly and claims weekly; data/ is reused only within a run.

redistribution.why: DOL data are U.S. government works in the public domain (17 U.S.C. 105). Enforcement records name employers (public records); the DOL API terms forbid sharing API keys, not data.

citation: U.S. Department of Labor, {dataset}, DOL Open Data API (apiprod.dol.gov/v4), retrieved {retrieved_long}.
clarify: Seasonally adjusted or not seasonally adjusted claims? The weekly national table has both (c5/c7 adjusted, c4/c6 not); state tables are not seasonally adjusted.
Enforcement counts measure enforcement activity, not violations in the economy: report them as inspections or cases found, by the date field used (open date, issuance date, findings end date).
